pageCache.pageTitle: Brimscombe C of E Primary School - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
It is my absolute pleasure to welcome you and your family to Brimscombe C of E (VA) Primary School. Whether you are joining us for the first time or are already part of our wonderful school community, I am delighted to have the opportunity to share with you what makes our school such a special place.
At the heart of everything we do is our school vision:
This simple yet powerful statement guides our daily work with children, shaping how we teach, how we interact, and how we support every member of our school family.
Our vision comes to life through our five core values:
Kindness – We encourage children to show compassion and care for others, creating a warm and supportive environment where everyone feels valued. Courage – We inspire children to be brave, to try new things, and to persevere when faced with challenges. Respect – We teach children to value themselves, others, and the world around them. Responsibility – We help children understand the importance of taking ownership of their actions and making positive choices. Friendship – We foster strong, supportive relationships that help children feel they belong and can thrive.
These values are woven into every aspect of school life – from our curriculum and assemblies to how we celebrate achievements and address challenges. We believe that by nurturing these qualities alongside academic excellence, we are preparing children not just for the next stage of their education, but for life.
As a Church of England school, our Christian foundation enriches our ethos and provides a strong moral framework. We welcome families of all faiths and none, united by our shared commitment to love, kindness, and respect. Our close links with the local church and our regular collective worship help children explore important questions about values, community, and what it means to live well together.
Your involvement in your child's education makes a real difference. We warmly encourage you to engage with school life – whether that's supporting learning at home, attending events, or simply keeping in touch with your child's teacher. Our door is always open, and we welcome your questions, ideas, and feedback.
I look forward to getting to know you and your family, and to working together to ensure your child has a wonderful experience at Brimscombe. Together, with love and kindness as our motivation, we will help every child flourish.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimscombe C of E Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our shared vision is what makes Brimscombe C of E (VA) School such an inclusive and happy place. Rooted in Christian Values, it is at the heart of all we do. It is taken firstly from Paul’s letter to the Corinthians.
‘Stay alert and hold firmly to all you believe. Be mighty and full of courage. Let love and kindness be the motivation behind all that you do.'
1 Corinthians 16:13-14
Through our Christian ethos, we nurture enquiring minds, a spirit of curiosity, resilience, and respect for others. Every member of our school community is valued and celebrated for who they are. By fostering positive relationships, offering challenge and support, and striving for excellence, we aim to help each child flourish—academically, socially, and spiritually.
The school's associated values for life, include their spiritual, moral and social culture are also an integral part of the foundation of what we do and are promoted and celebrated through the whole curriculum.
Our values for life are:
Kindness, Courage, Respect, Responsibility and Friendship
Vision and Values

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimscombe C of E Primary School - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values
The Department of Education have reinforced the need "to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs"
The Government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent strategy, In our school these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways
Many activities across the curriculum have outcomes that are voted for by the pupils including voting for choice of class rewards when awarded whole class / group rewards. Pupils use their voices to debate and make decisions. Fairness and equity of opportunity are championed by our staff and unfairness is challenged
The importance of Laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout the regular school days, as well as when dealing with behaviour and through school worship. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from and to authorities such as the Police & Fire Service are regular parts of our calendar and help reinforce this message.
Within school, pupils are actively encouraged to make choice, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for young pupils to make choices safety, through the provision of safe environment and empowering education. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and advise how to exercise these safely, for example through our E-Safety and PHSE lessons. Whether it be through choice of challenge, of how they record, of participation in our numerous extra-curricular clubs and opportunities, pupils are given the freedom to make choices.
A core element of our ethos focuses on respect which is one of our values for life. During worship, PSHE, RE and informal daily discussions, mutual respect is reinforced and discussed. Respect for others and their property is promoted through our classroom rules, as well as our behaviour policy.
We are a school where the importance of tolerance, understanding and kindness are taught with skill and dedication and integrated into every aspect of school life. For example through Christian values themed worship; through focusing and raising money for charities in UK and overseas aid; through the development of pupils to lead and care for one another; through bringing parents together to meet and learn as part of our school community; through emphasising the importance of knowing about and celebrating each other's differences in order to remove stereotypes and barriers.
Modern British Values are interwoven into the daily lives of our school's learning community and are naturally reflected through everything we do.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimscombe C of E Primary School - Our Church
pageCache.text:
Our Church
As a Church of England school, we are linked and supported by the church family at Holy Trinity, Brimscombe. This church is part of the benefice of two other churches, St Mary's, Woodchester and St Mary Magdalen, Rodborough. Our minister and lay readers join us for celebration services linked to the Church of England calendar events and lead and share worship with our children at school.
Our Open the Book team lead school assemblies each week, bringing Bible stories to life.
We invite the school to visit the church during the academic year to enhance their RSE curriculum and also enjoy whole school church services at Christmas and on occasion at Easter.
In addition, as a church school we have Foundation Governors who support and uphold the Vision and Values of the school, whilst diligently helping the school be the very best it can be and offer all children the best education.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimscombe C of E Primary School - MFL - French
pageCache.text:
MFL - French
'Stay alert and hold firmly to all you believe. Be mighty and full of courage. Let love and kindness be the motivation behind all that you do.'
1 Corinthians 16:13-14
Curriculum
Bonjour! Welcome to French at Brimscombe
At Brimscombe C of E (VA) Primary School, we want our children to develop a love of languages and an enthusiasm for discovering other cultures and our French curriculum is shaped by our Christian vision, which encourages courage, curiosity, and compassion. Children learn to communicate in a new language, while developing their listening, speaking, reading and writing skills in French.
Our French curriculum is carefully sequenced across the school so that children revisit and build on their learning each year. Lessons are active, practical and engaging, with opportunities for children to sing, speak, play games, take part in conversations and explore aspects of French culture.
Learning a language is about much more than vocabulary and grammar. Throughout our French curriculum, children are encouraged to discover the people, places, traditions, food and celebrations associated with France and the wider French-speaking world.
Children discover countries where French is spoken, learn about French food and celebrations, explore famous French people and historical figures. They develop an appreciation of cultural similarities and differences and begin to understand that French is a global language spoken in many parts of the world.
Our French curriculum is designed so that each stage prepares children for the next. Vocabulary and structures are regularly revisited, helping pupils to remember what they have learnt and use it in new contexts.
By the end of Year 6, we aim for children to have developed:
confidence in speaking and listening in French;
a growing bank of useful French vocabulary;
an understanding of simple French sentence structures;
an appreciation of French culture;
curiosity and enthusiasm for learning languages.
Teaching
Years 1 and 2 – Bonjour, ça va?
Our youngest learners begin by becoming familiar with the sounds and rhythms of French. They learn simple greetings and introductions, numbers, colours, family vocabulary and everyday classroom language.
Songs, games and repetition help children to develop an ear for the language while building their confidence to join in.
Children are also introduced to aspects of French culture. They learn about celebrations such as Christmas and Easter in France, explore French foods and begin to recognise some of the similarities and differences between life in France and life in the UK.
Years 3 and 4 – Having a go
As children move through Key Stage 2, they build on their earlier knowledge and begin to use French more independently.
The children will revisit familiar vocabulary, while extending their knowledge of numbers, colours, animals, family members, food and everyday classroom language, while developing their ability to ask and answer simple questions and express their likes and dislikes.
Reading and writing are introduced alongside speaking and listening, so children begin to see how the different strands of language work together.
Pupils explore French-speaking countries around Europe and the rest of the world, French traditions and celebrations, French history, through learning about The French Revolution and more.
Years 5 and 6 – Finding our voice
By Years 5 and 6, pupils are ready to use their French with greater independence. They revisit and consolidate previous vocabulary, while learning to construct longer phrases and sentences.
Topics include family, pets, food, hobbies, the body, clothing, weather and everyday activities. Children develop their ability to describe themselves and others, express likes and dislikes, ask and answer questions and understand simple spoken and written French.
They also begin to recognise and use grammatical structures, including masculine and feminine nouns, simple verbs and sentence patterns. Regular retrieval activities help children remember and apply vocabulary from previous years.
Achievement
By the time our children leave Brimscombe, each child will gain confidence that they can try to communicate in another language. Most importantly, we hope our children leave us with curiosity about the wider world and the confidence to step into it.
“Bonjour!” is just the beginning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimscombe C of E Primary School - Personal Development and Wellbeing
pageCache.text:
Personal Development and Wellbeing
Personal development and wellbeing is woven through everyday life at Brimscombe and supports pupils to grow as confident, thoughtful members of the community. Pupils are given real opportunities to take responsibility and contribute to school life through groups such as Pupil Council and Eco Committee, where they learn to listen, debate ideas and make decisions that improve their school environment.
Our approach is underpinned by the promotion of British Values, including democracy, mutual respect, tolerance and the rule of law. Alongside this, we place strong emphasis on pupils' social, moral and cultural development. Through assemblies, classroom discussion, community projects and enrichment activities, pupils are encouraged to reflect on their actions, understand different perspectives and develop a strong sense of responsibility towards others and the wider world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimscombe C of E Primary School - PSHE & RSE
pageCache.text:
PSHE & RSE
Stay alert and hold firmly to all you believe. Be mighty and full of courage. Let love and kindness be the motivation behind all that you do.'
1 Corinthians 16:13-14
Our PSHE/RSE curriculum covers the full breadth of learning pupils need to stay healthy, safe and prepared for life. This includes:
PSHE & RSE education helps pupils maintain their mental and physical health and understand the various factors that influence their wellbeing. They learn how to build strong and supportive relationships, how to keep themselves safe in various situations and how to make thoughtful decisions about money, health and the online world.
Pupils may receive mixed messages about these topics from friends, siblings, social media and the wider world. High-quality RSE & PSHE ensures every child receives clear, accurate and age-appropriate teaching so they can make safe and informed choices as they grow.
Our PSHE/RSE curriculum is organised into strands and key areas to ensure a broad and balanced curriculum.
Key areas group learning into meaningful themes and ensure that all statutory content is covered. The strands weave throughout all units, demonstrating how pupils develop lifelong skills in managing themselves, regulating their emotions, building positive relationships and thinking critically.
Together, the strands and key areas help pupils revisit important ideas over time, building their confidence and understanding in a structured way.
Some key areas are revisited each year, while others are revisited less frequently to reflect the volume of content in the statutory guidance and ensure learning is age-appropriate.
PSHE/RSE is taught for 45 minutes per week. This allows sufficient time to meet the DfE’s Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education guidance. This recommendation is also informed by market research, which shows that many schools structure their RSE & PSHE provision in this way.
In addition to discrete lessons, PSHE & RSE learning is often reinforced through day-to-day school life. Teachers will naturally revisit and apply their learning in response to real-life situations that arise, such as issues on the playground, in the classroom or during discussions, helping pupils to make meaningful links between taught content and real experiences.
The RSHE statutory guidance requires schools to:
In PSHE & RSE, pupil outcomes go beyond pupils being able to recall key knowledge or demonstrate specific skills in the classroom. The curriculum is designed to support pupils’ confidence, wellbeing and the way they interact with others in everyday situations.
These aspects of learning develop gradually over time and can be harder to measure. When taught consistently as part of a well-sequenced curriculum, schools may notice changes in pupils’ attitudes, choices and behaviour across school life.
Over time, pupils may show increased confidence in expressing feelings, asking for help and making decisions. They begin to develop self-awareness and emotional literacy, which supports resilience when facing challenges or change.
Pupils may become better able to manage behaviour and responses, especially in challenging situations. They gain an understanding of why rules are vital for ensuring their own safety and that of others, and learn how to follow them.
Over time, pupils can develop resilience by learning to cope with setbacks, manage their emotions, make amends and move forward positively, thereby supporting a calm and safe school environment.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimscombe C of E Primary School - Religious Education
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
'Stay alert and hold firmly to all you believe. Be mighty and full of courage. Let love and kindness be the motivation behind all that you do.'
1 Corinthians 16:13-14
Brimscombe CE VA Primary School was founded by the Church of England in 1840 to provide education to children in the area. The original school was housed just below Holy Trinity Church on Brimscombe Hill. The new school was opened in 1997. The facilities here are modern but we hold dear our traditional values and Christian ethos.
Through the high quality teaching of Religious Education at Brimscombe, we aim to:
At Brimscombe C of E Primary School, Religious Education is taught through the Gloucestershire Agreed Syllabus for RE 2025-2030, following a Religion and Worldviews (RW) approach. Pupils explore a range of religious and non-religious worldviews, including Christianity, Judaism, Islam, Hinduism and Humanism, alongside thematic units that encourage reflection on life's big questions. The curriculum is carefully sequenced through a rolling programme, enabling pupils to revisit and deepen their understanding of key concepts as they progress through the school. As a Church of England school, pupils also explore the theological concepts of Creation, God, People of God, Incarnation, Gospel, Salvation and Kingdom of God. Through RE, children develop their understanding of how beliefs and worldviews influence people's lives, while also reflecting on their own values, beliefs and experiences.
Our RE curriculum encourages pupils to think deeply, ask meaningful questions and engage thoughtfully with different beliefs and perspectives. Lessons are structured around key enquiry questions and are underpinned by the syllabus' threefold aim: understanding how worldviews influence people's lives, engaging with these worldviews in thoughtful and scholarly ways, and developing understanding of themselves and others. Pupils are introduced to different "Ways of Knowing", helping them consider how knowledge is gained and interpreted within different traditions. Learning is supported through discussion, visits, visitors, artefacts, stories, texts and reflective activities that bring worldviews to life.
Religious Education is taught weekly and is a core subject at Brimscombe C of E Primary School.
Assessment in RE focuses on pupils' developing knowledge, understanding and ability to engage thoughtfully with religious and non-religious worldviews. Teachers use questioning, discussion, written work and reflective responses to assess pupils' understanding throughout each unit. Regular retrieval activities, learning logs and opportunities to revisit prior learning enable teachers to monitor how well pupils retain and apply key concepts over time. Assessment is informed by the enquiry-based nature of the curriculum and considers pupils' ability to explain beliefs and practices, make connections between different worldviews and reflect on their own ideas and experiences. Through ongoing assessment, teachers ensure that all pupils make progress in their understanding of religion, belief and the diverse communities that make up our local, national and global society.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimscombe C of E Primary School - School Opening Hours
pageCache.text:
School Opening Hours
The school is open from 8.00am for those families who have booked their children in for early morning care.
Class teachers welcome the children into school at 8:45am where they prepare for the day and complete morning tasks.
Registration takes place between 8:55-9:00am. Lessons begin promptly at 9:00am.
The school day ends for preschool at 3:00pm and the rest of the school at 3:15pm.
Extra-curricular clubs run by members of staff and outside groups are from 3:15-4:15pm.
Our after school wrap-around care is provided by Atlas Camps and runs from 3:15pm-6:00pm.
The total time in a typical week is 32.5 hours - 8:45am to 3.15pm excluding preschool
School Opening Hours
